name: MYCEL-8
author: David Ryan
tagline: eight generative parts: Euclid rhythms, Turing pitch
description: MYCEL-8 grows music from a few numbers. Eight parts each have a Euclidean rhythm (steps, pulses, rotate, division) and a Turing-machine shift register that picks notes from a pool of scale degrees chosen on the white keys: locked it loops, unlocked it drifts. Chance, accents, ratchets, a density and tide macro, dice with a history to go back to, a lock, and eight snapshots recalled at the bar. Its own synth and drums, and MIDI out over USB and Bluetooth.
credits: Built on fm1-base and felucca-bsp, from Felucca by Leo Kuroshita (Hügelton Instruments). After the Music Thing Turing Machine, Euclidean rhythms (Toussaint) and the Torso T-1. Fonts: Barlow (SIL OFL 1.1).
